3.6.5.name: scripts.task_manager._activate_copilot_window
3.6.5.description: Trace a Ready task's recorded worker session (pid + window title) and re-focus the still-running Copilot console window for review; returns False when the window is no longer traceable.

3.6.6.name: scripts.task_manager._build_review_prompt
3.6.6.description: Build a review-focused Copilot prompt for a Ready task from build/instructions/task-review.md, used to start a dedicated review session when the worker window is not traceable.

3.6.7.name: scripts.task_manager._delete_task
3.6.7.description: Soft-delete a task by moving it to the 'Deleted' status, or permanently remove it from the task list when it is already deleted; exposed via the DELETE /api/tasks/<id> endpoint with a dedicated Deleted tab in the UI, while deleted tasks are restricted to status-only modifications.

3.6.8.name: scripts.task_manager._sync_selected_app_on_startup
3.6.8.description: On task manager UI startup, automatically sync only the currently selected app's task file with its own linked git repo before the task list is served, reusing the git sync helper with wait=True: on Windows it opens a visible console window for the sync and blocks until it completes; the sync is skipped when no git repo is linked and any failure is reported but never blocks startup. Skippable via the --no-startup-sync CLI flag.

3.6.9.name: scripts.task_manager._status_inbox_dir
3.6.9.description: Resolve and create the durable 'task status store' directory layout (pending/processed/failed) used by the file-store status channel. The root and poll interval are configurable via APP.TASK_MANAGER.status_queue / request_polling_frequency / enable (status_queue defaults under OUTPUT_PATH); the pending area is the same location surfaced to agents via the {status_store} placeholder in the task.md prompt. Returns None when the channel is disabled or unconfigured. Helper _resolve_status_store_paths reads the config and computes the layout.

3.6.10.name: scripts.task_manager._process_status_inbox
3.6.10.description: Scan the pending area of the task status store for agent-written request files (each a {"TASKS":[...]} document restricted to id/status/comments/worker_session), apply each to a freshly loaded ledger via _apply_task_update (matched by task id), persist the ledger, then stage/commit/push it to main headlessly via _sync_task_store_to_git(headless=True); move each request file to processed/ on success or failed/ on error. Helper _apply_status_request_file performs the per-file apply+sync. Each file is processed exactly once (idempotent, restart-safe); a git-sync failure is logged but does not re-fail the request (avoiding duplicate comment appends).

3.6.11.name: scripts.task_manager._status_inbox_watcher
3.6.11.description: Background daemon thread, started by run() (skippable via --no-status-inbox), that continuously samples the live store at the configured APP.TASK_MANAGER.request_polling_frequency interval by calling _process_status_inbox, so status/comment requests written by agents (including while the server was previously down) are applied to the ledger on main without blocking the agent.

3.6.12.name: scripts.task_manager._apply_task_update
3.6.12.description: Apply one update task (matched by id within the in-memory TASKS list, restricted to status/comments/worker_session) onto the ledger by value type via the recursive helper _apply_task_fields: list fields (comments) combine existing+incoming, dict fields (worker_session) update recursively, scalar fields (status) overwrite; comments are normalised before being appended. Returns None when no task matches the id. Replaces a generic deep-merge because TASKS is a list keyed by id.

3.6.13.name: scripts.status_queue_mcp
3.6.13.description: Per-agent stdio MCP server (a thin 'enqueue' writer over the durable task status store) launched by launch_task_agent.ps1 via the Copilot CLI --additional-mcp-config hook, so its lifecycle is bound to one worker agent. It exposes a single tool, enqueue_status_update(status?, comment?), that builds a restricted {"TASKS":[{id,status,comments}]} request (the task id and default comment author come from env vars TASK_STATUS_TASK_ID/TASK_STATUS_AUTHOR) and writes it atomically (temp-then-rename) into the store's pending directory (TASK_STATUS_PENDING_DIR) -- the same files _process_status_inbox consumes. The server is stateless and holds no in-memory queue (restart-safe) and is never on the critical path: if it is unavailable the agent falls back to writing the request file directly. Dequeue is deliberately not implemented here because the Task Manager consumes the shared store directly from the filesystem. Transport is newline-delimited JSON-RPC 2.0 over stdio (initialize/tools/list/tools/call/ping); diagnostics go to stderr. Pure functions build_status_update_request/write_request_atomically and the _dispatch handler are unit-tested.

3.6.13.1.name: scripts.status_queue_mcp.build_status_update_request
3.6.13.1.description: Build a restricted {"TASKS":[{id,status?,comments?}]} update request for one task id, including only the supplied fields (status overwrites; a single comment is appended). Raises ValueError when neither status nor comment is provided.

3.6.13.2.name: scripts.status_queue_mcp.write_request_atomically
3.6.13.2.description: Write a request dict as a uniquely named JSON file into the store's pending directory using a temp-then-rename so the Task Manager never reads a half-written request. Returns the final file path.

3.6.13.3.name: scripts.status_queue_mcp.main
3.6.13.3.description: Entry point: run the newline-delimited JSON-RPC 2.0 stdio loop, decoding each line and dispatching initialize/tools/list/tools/call/ping until stdin closes.

3.6.14.name: scripts.task_manager._write_agent_mcp_config
3.6.14.description: When the durable status store is enabled, write a per-agent MCP config file ({"mcpServers":{"task-status-queue":{type:local,command:python,args:[status_queue_mcp.py],env:{TASK_STATUS_PENDING_DIR,TASK_STATUS_TASK_ID,TASK_STATUS_AUTHOR},tools:[*]}}}) next to the agent prompt and return its path; _start_copilot_for_task passes it to launch_task_agent.ps1 via -McpConfig, which appends --additional-mcp-config @<path> to the Copilot CLI invocation. Returns None when the status store is disabled/unconfigured (the agent then uses the documented direct-file-write fallback).

3.7.name: scripts.sync_task_repo
3.7.description: PowerShell helper that commits and pushes ONLY the task ledger (build/tasks/<app>.json) to the linked git remote, fully isolated from the worker's primary working tree. It takes an optional -Branch parameter (the ledger branch; defaults to the current HEAD branch, and the headless status-inbox sync passes the configured APP.TASK_MANAGER.ledger_branch, default main). It reads the server-updated ledger content from the primary working tree and applies it inside a dedicated, reusable DETACHED git worktree built from the latest origin/<branch> tip, where it path-scopes the change with 'git add -- <ledger>', commits with the provided message, and pushes to refs/heads/<branch>; on a non-fast-forward push it fetches and rebases the single ledger commit inside that isolated worktree (which only ever contains the ledger change) and retries. It never runs 'git add -A'/'commit -a' and never stages, commits, stashes, rebases (autostash), or otherwise touches the worker's primary working tree, so it cannot sweep the worker's uncommitted code into the server's commits, push worker code ahead of the approval gate, or drop uncommitted worker changes. Invoked by the task manager UI Sync Git button, the automatic startup sync, and the headless status-inbox sync.

6.1.11.name: utils.baseutils.AppManager
6.1.11.description: Main runtime lifecycle class that loads inputs, processes data, stores outputs, and finalizes run state.

6.1.11.1.name: utils.baseutils.AppManager.load_data
6.1.11.1.description: Load all enabled config.input entries into results targets; persists per-input last_modified maps in self.input_meta to support DataLoader delta mode across cycles.

6.1.11.2.name: utils.baseutils.AppManager.process_data
6.1.11.2.description: Run configured processing steps against loaded results data.

6.1.11.3.name: utils.baseutils.AppManager.store_outputs
6.1.11.3.description: Persist configured outputs sequentially or concurrently via ThreadPoolExecutor based on CONFIG.COMMON.OUTPUT_WORKERS. Supports split artifacts and output-level delta flag backed by a sha256 checksum manifest. Per-worker exceptions are caught and logged as BASEW06 without aborting remaining writes.

6.1.11.4.name: utils.baseutils.AppManager.close
6.1.11.4.description: Finalize the run state and prepare runtime artifacts for saving.

6.1.11.5.name: utils.baseutils.AppManager.run
6.1.11.5.description: Run the full data loading and processing pipeline, then store outputs.

6.1.11.6.name: utils.baseutils.AppManager.create_results
6.1.11.6.description: Initialize the in-memory results container that holds per-target loaded and processed data.

6.1.11.7.name: utils.baseutils.AppManager.touch_result
6.1.11.7.description: Update a result target's last-modified timestamp from a source descriptor.

6.1.11.8.name: utils.baseutils.AppManager.open_output
6.1.11.8.description: Open a previously saved output artifact for a given output key.

6.1.11.9.name: utils.baseutils.AppManager._store_one_output
6.1.11.9.description: Resolve, convert, and persist a single configured output artifact; callable from both sequential loop and ThreadPoolExecutor worker threads in store_outputs. Returns a flat list of stored file paths.

6.1.11.10.name: utils.baseutils.AppManager.OUTPUT_MAP
6.1.11.10.description: Manager attribute initialised as an empty dict in AppManager.__init__ and deep-updated by every store_outputs call with {output_key: [file_paths]}. Never reset between calls so successive calls accumulate entries. Returned by store_outputs so callers can use the mapping directly.

6.2.name: utils.datautils
6.2.description: Data conversion and file loading utilities used by the runtime pipeline.

6.2.1.name: utils.datautils.DataConverter
6.2.1.description: Securely applies transformation rules to a pandas DataFrame. Supports col, row, df, and custom scopes with per-step exception handling; logs DATAE01 for all step failures (including missing source column) and collects them in self.errors.

6.2.1.1.name: utils.datautils.DataConverter.apply
6.2.1.1.description: Apply the configured transformation rules to a pandas DataFrame and return the result. Supports a 'custom' scope that evaluates the op expression against the converter's context dict and returns the raw result directly, bypassing the DataFrame column-assignment path. Each step is wrapped in try-except; all exceptions (including missing source column KeyError) are logged via DATAE01 and collected in self.errors.

6.2.2.name: utils.datautils.DataLoader
6.2.2.description: Load files from a source file or folder using configurable format and optional logging. Supports an input-level `delta` flag: in delta mode the loader rescans the source on every call and only loads files that are new or whose on-disk mtime changed since the previous load, tracking per-file mtimes in last_modified.

6.2.2.1.name: utils.datautils.DataLoader.load
6.2.2.1.description: Load files from the configured source (file or folder), honoring delta mode and updating last_modified.

6.3.1.2.name: utils.testutils.TestManager.request_store
6.3.1.2.description: Queue an arbitrary item for storage in the test results bundle.

6.3.1.3.description: Run all tests defined for the given phase (prep, live, or post).

6.3.1.4.description: Start the background live-monitoring loop that periodically evaluates live tests.

6.3.1.5.description: Stop the background live-monitoring loop and join the worker thread.

6.3.1.6.description: Finalize test run state and persist accumulated results.

6.3.1.7.name: utils.testutils.TestManager.run_a_test
6.3.1.7.description: Execute a single test definition for the given phase and record the outcome.

6.3.2.name: utils.testutils.build_test_config
6.3.2.description: Build runtime test configuration by combining integrated app config with the testing base config.

6.3.3.name: utils.testutils.evaluate_checks
6.3.3.description: Evaluate declarative checks and return structured pass or fail results.

6.3.4.name: utils.testutils.monitor_activity
6.3.4.description: Validate that runtime monitoring produced the expected amount of activity.

6.3.5.name: utils.testutils.test_deployment
6.3.5.description: Run a PowerShell deployment test script non-interactively, parse each [PASS]/[FAIL]/[WARN] output line as a criterion, and return a structured result dict compatible with TestManager.

6.3.6.name: utils.testutils.mcp_server_status
6.3.6.description: Live test that health-checks ALL per-agent status-queue MCP servers as one aggregate test and reports their active rate. It discovers every configured server from the per-agent <task-id>.mcp.json files in APP.TASK_MANAGER.prompt_store (via _discover_mcp_servers; falling back to the canonical scripts/status_queue_mcp.py when idle), spawns each as a fresh subprocess and verifies an MCP initialize handshake (a server is 'up' when it returns a well-formed serverInfo result) via the helper _probe_mcp_command, and counts the pending status-queue depth via _resolve_status_queue_pending. It reports servers up/down and the active rate (up/total), logging the single aggregate result to the console as GOOD when none are down, WARN when exactly one is down/unresponsive, and FAIL when more than one is down. Registered as the live_mcp_server_status live test sampled every 60 seconds. _probe_mcp_server remains a thin script-path wrapper over _probe_mcp_command.
